summary: Feed s113_double is degraded: 2 faults detected. 78.3% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS tolerance (60%) and 8.3% of frames are sliced to ~256 bytes, both reducing IDS payload visibility and detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: 78.3% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/encrypted) vs 60% IDS tolerance. Packet broker is forwarding encrypted traffic without decryption/SSL visibility, likely no decrypt policy or keys installed before the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect payloads inside encryption; signatures and anomaly detection are blind to ~78% of traffic, allowing threats to hide in encrypted flows and reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload for inspection; decrypt relevant TLS at broker/proxy or route a decrypted copy to IDS to bring encrypted share below 60% tolerance

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing is enabled and cutting frames to ~256 bytes. 143 of 1728 frames (8.3%) are truncated, exceeding 5% threshold. IDS requires full payload but is receiving sliced packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with needs_full_payload=true cannot perform full signature matching, reassembly, or file extraction on truncated frames; attacks beyond 256 bytes are missed and alerts are incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing / set snaplen to 0 or >=1518 bytes for this IDS feed so full payload is delivered within its 1518-byte MTU, restoring detection capability
